geo.title: Get started

Biggest round table in a triangular room.

Goal: I can construct a triangle's inscribed circle.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Theorem: the angle bisectors of a triangle meet at one point, the incenter, which is the same distance from all three sides.

Proof: a point inside an angle is on its bisector exactly when it is equidistant from the angle's sides. The point I where two bisectors cross is equidistant from all three sides, so it is on the third bisector too.

That common distance is the radius of the inscribed circle, tangent to all three sides. The incenter is always inside the triangle. To draw the incircle, drop a perpendicular from I to one side to get the radius.
